change: Restructured primary/secondary. Removed 'Lats' (Latissimus Dorsi + Rotator Cuff) from primary — in this arm-only yoga stretch the lats are not a prime-mover primary target; they are secondary (the bottom arm requires lats to be flexible and rotator cuff for joint stability). Moved 'shoulders' (Posterior Deltoid) from secondary to primary — the bottom arm strongly stretches the posterior deltoid (shoulder extension + internal rotation), making it a primary stretch target alongside the triceps. Removed 'chest' (Clavicular Head) secondary — sources describe pectoral flexibility as a prerequisite for the pose, not a primary stretch target; chest is not a well-documented stretch target for this arm-only variation.

Moved 'Lateral Deltoids' from primary to secondary and merged into a separate secondary shoulders entry. In pike position the Anterior Deltoids are the primary weight-bearing shoulder muscles; Lateral Deltoids are stabilizers (secondary). The primary shoulders entry now contains only Anterior Deltoids. A new secondary shoulders entry with Lateral Deltoids was added.

Removed 'Lower Back' (Erector Spinae) from secondary. Web sources consistently identify the primary stretch targets as glutes, hip flexors (Rectus Femoris), and adductors. Erector Spinae is not cited as a meaningful target in pigeon pose — it may be passively involved in the folded-forward variation but is not a reliable secondary stretch across the general pose.

Moved 'Lateral Deltoids' from primary to secondary and placed in a separate secondary shoulders entry alongside Anterior Deltoids (which remain primary). In pike position, Anterior Deltoids bear the load; Lateral Deltoids are stabilizers. Primary shoulders entry now contains only Anterior Deltoids.

Same correction as pike_alternating_opposite_hip_taps: moved 'Lateral Deltoids' from primary to secondary. In pike position (and especially when reaching one arm forward/overhead), Anterior Deltoids are the prime movers; Lateral Deltoids are secondary stabilizers.
